name: GE Vernova
thesis: Broad power-scarcity play spanning gas turbines, grid equipment and electrification. Benefits from AI/data-centre load growth without depending on one chip vendor.
catalysts: Large gas and grid backlog; capacity expansion; utility and data-centre power demand.
risks: Premium valuation, turbine execution and a capex slowdown could compress the multiple.
researchNote: One of the strongest cross-theme names because it sits between generation and the grid.

name: BWX Technologies
thesis: Actual nuclear earnings from naval, government and commercial nuclear programs rather than reactor-startup optionality.
catalysts: Large backlog, commercial nuclear expansion and US defence/nuclear investment.
risks: Premium valuation, government program timing and capacity-expansion execution.
researchNote: Best risk-adjusted nuclear name in the current basket.

name: China Resources Power
thesis: Lower-multiple way to own rising electricity demand through thermal plus renewable generation.
catalysts: Power demand growth, renewable additions, fuel-cost normalisation and valuation rerating.
risks: Chinese tariffs, coal economics, policy intervention and capital intensity.
researchNote: One of the cleaner valuation + power-demand combinations in HK.

name: Tenaga Nasional
thesis: The boring end of the AI trade: data centres can change chips and vendors but still require electricity and grid capacity.
catalysts: New data-centre connections, regulated asset growth and Malaysian grid capex.
risks: Regulation, fuel-cost recovery and national policy.
researchNote: Portfolio ballast against higher-beta Malaysian data-centre names.

name: Quanta Services
thesis: Builds the physical transmission, substation and utility infrastructure required by electrification and large-load interconnections.
catalysts: Record backlog, grid hardening, transmission expansion and data-centre interconnections.
risks: Project execution, labour costs and premium valuation.
researchNote: High-quality picks-and-shovels exposure further away from GPU-cycle risk.

name: Eaton
thesis: Electrical distribution bottleneck between generation and the rack: switchgear, breakers, busway and power-management equipment.
catalysts: Data-centre orders, electrical backlog and industrial electrification.
risks: AI enthusiasm is embedded in valuation; a capex slowdown could hit both earnings expectations and the multiple.
researchNote: Excellent business; entry price matters.

name: CGN Power
thesis: Operating-reactor exposure with recurring generation revenue and state-backed nuclear buildout rather than development-stage SMR risk.
catalysts: New-unit commissioning, capacity additions and China's long-term nuclear buildout.
risks: Tariff policy, reactor outages, capex and SOE governance discount.
researchNote: Direct China nuclear utility expression.

name: Exxon Mobil
thesis: High-quality broad oil exposure with advantaged upstream barrels, refining, chemicals and large-scale capital returns.
catalysts: Guyana, Permian growth, structural cost reductions, LNG and shareholder returns.
risks: Oil-price downside, refining-margin compression and global recession.
researchNote: Core cyclical oil holding when valuation and oil-price setup are sensible.

name: Williams Companies
thesis: Indirect AI-power exposure through gas infrastructure feeding power generation, LNG and industrial demand.
catalysts: US gas demand growth, power-generation load and pipeline/storage projects.
risks: Permitting, leverage and slower long-term gas demand.
researchNote: One of the best AI-power crossovers without owning AI hardware.

name: Southern Cable
thesis: Cable is a hard physical requirement for grid upgrades and data centres, while TNB-related spending broadens demand beyond AI.
catalysts: High-voltage certification, TNB orders and Malaysian data-centre grid expansion.
risks: Copper input costs, project margins and small-cap valuation risk.
researchNote: One of the cleaner Malaysia picks-and-shovels names.

name: YTL Power
thesis: Direct Malaysian AI-infrastructure expression combining data centres, generation and cloud exposure.
catalysts: Contracted data-centre capacity, Kulai expansion and AI-cloud monetisation.
risks: AI/data-centre narrative sensitivity, capex intensity and execution.
researchNote: Higher upside and higher theme sensitivity than TNB.

name: Centrus Energy
thesis: Strategically scarce US enrichment and HALEU capacity tied to energy security and domestic nuclear fuel policy.
catalysts: US enrichment awards, HALEU scale-up and nuclear-fuel reshoring.
risks: Government-contract dependence, execution and valuation volatility.
researchNote: Scarcity infrastructure rather than generic uranium beta.

name: Cameco
thesis: Higher-quality uranium exposure with operating assets and Westinghouse participation.
catalysts: Long-term contracting, uranium supply tightness, reactor restarts/new builds and Westinghouse growth.
risks: Uranium cycle, mine execution and premium valuation.
researchNote: Core nuclear-fuel watch rather than a startup bet.

name: Dongfang Electric
thesis: Broad Chinese power-equipment manufacturer spanning turbines, generators and energy equipment across nuclear, hydro and thermal buildout.
catalysts: China generation buildout, equipment localisation and nuclear/hydro expansion.
risks: SOE economics, project margins and policy-driven capex cycles.
researchNote: Potentially one of the better HK power picks-and-shovels names.

name: CNOOC
thesis: Clean large-cap Chinese upstream oil expression with low-cost offshore production and international assets.
catalysts: Production growth in China and overseas projects including Guyana.
risks: Oil cycle, SOE/geopolitical risk and project execution.
researchNote: Higher oil beta than PetroChina.

name: Chevron
thesis: High-quality integrated oil major with Permian, LNG and Guyana/Hess exposure.
catalysts: Hess integration, Guyana, Permian, LNG and capital returns.
risks: Oil cycle, project execution and integration risk.
researchNote: Compare directly with XOM on FCF yield, growth and valuation.

name: Sunway Construction
thesis: Direct Malaysian physical-buildout play with large data-centre construction exposure plus broader construction capabilities.
catalysts: Continued hyperscale project awards and MEP/data-centre execution.
risks: Capex slowdown, project concentration and construction execution.
researchNote: Higher AI sensitivity than TNB or cable/grid names.

name: MN Holdings
thesis: Pure picks-and-shovels exposure to high-voltage substations and grid connections for Malaysian data centres.
catalysts: Hyperscale electrical contracts and continued Johor/Klang Valley buildout.
risks: Small-cap execution, working capital, project concentration and AI-capex sensitivity.
researchNote: More direct DC exposure than TNB; less broad than Southern Cable.

name: Constellation Energy
thesis: Existing nuclear generation monetising scarce 24/7 power with far less technology risk than reactor-development stocks.
catalysts: Power demand, nuclear licence extensions, restarts and long-duration clean-power contracts.
risks: Power-price exposure, regulation and premium valuation.
researchNote: Direct AI + nuclear crossover with real operating assets.

name: Kinder Morgan
thesis: Fee-based gas infrastructure exposure to LNG, power generation and industrial demand.
catalysts: Natural-gas project backlog and rising power-generation demand.
risks: Permitting, debt and slower long-term gas growth.
researchNote: Steadier than high-beta power names.

name: Cheniere Energy
thesis: Owns the US LNG export toll-booth layer, driven by global gas contracting and energy security rather than AI.
catalysts: Long-term contracts, LNG capacity and Europe/Asia demand.
risks: Future LNG oversupply, feedgas costs, construction and regulation.
researchNote: Cleaner global-gas infrastructure exposure than upstream producers.

name: PETRONAS Gas
thesis: Lower-beta Malaysian gas infrastructure with processing, transmission and utility economics.
catalysts: Stable contracted infrastructure economics and Malaysian industrial/gas demand.
risks: Regulatory returns, maintenance outages and slower growth.
researchNote: Portfolio ballast against Hibiscus/YTL/NationGate-type cyclicality.

name: nVent Electric
thesis: Electrical connection/protection plus expanding liquid-cooling exposure for high-density AI infrastructure.
catalysts: Liquid-cooling deployment, AI reference architectures and electrical growth.
risks: AI capex sensitivity, integration and valuation.
researchNote: Middle ground between ETN diversification and VRT purity.

name: Vertiv
thesis: High-purity data-centre infrastructure through UPS, power distribution and cooling.
catalysts: AI rack density, cooling demand and hyperscaler buildout.
risks: A hyperscaler capex reset would hit both orders and valuation hard.
researchNote: Deliberate high-beta AI infrastructure sleeve, not a defensive electrical name.

name: Comfort Systems USA
thesis: Large facilities still need HVAC, piping, electrical systems and modular construction regardless of chip vendor.
catalysts: Mission-critical/data-centre construction and nationwide mechanical/electrical demand.
risks: Data-centre capex exposure, labour constraints and valuation.
researchNote: Less obvious physical-buildout beneficiary.

name: PetroChina
thesis: Broader integrated Chinese energy exposure than CNOOC with upstream, gas, refining and chemicals.
catalysts: Gas demand, upstream production and refining profitability.
risks: State pricing/policy, commodity cycles and SOE discount.
researchNote: Less pure oil beta than CNOOC; more diversified earnings drivers.

name: Enphase Energy
thesis: Premium microinverter and home-energy ecosystem with strong balance sheet but subsidy-sensitive earnings; data-centre power conversion is optionality.
catalysts: Core solar recovery, battery reacceleration, Europe bottoming and solid-state transformer progress.
risks: Residential solar weakness, policy incentives, customer concentration and stock compensation.
researchNote: Potential 3–5 year turnaround, but current earnings quality needs caution.

name: CGN Mining
thesis: Direct uranium-cycle exposure through natural-uranium trading and interests in Kazakh production assets.
catalysts: China reactor buildout, uranium contracting and production growth.
risks: Valuation, uranium trading margins and Kazakhstan/China geopolitical risk.
researchNote: Prefer consolidation rather than chasing a stretched bounce.

name: Oklo
thesis: Ambitious owner/operator reactor model with fuel recycling and recurring power-sale economics if commercial Aurora plants succeed.
catalysts: Regulatory progress, fuel availability, customer agreements and first commercial deployments.
risks: No operating commercial Aurora fleet yet; valuation rests on future plants.
researchNote: Prefer the business model to NuScale, but still venture-capital-like risk.

name: NuScale Power
thesis: US regulatory credential is valuable, but the investment still depends on converting approvals and discussions into financed operating projects.
catalysts: Binding PPAs, Romania project progress and commercial deployment.
risks: Pre-revenue economics, financing, dilution and project delays.
researchNote: Publicly traded nuclear venture capital until binding commercial projects de-risk it.

name: China Longyuan Power
thesis: Large Chinese renewable generator, but tariff/utilisation pressure weakens the economics versus broader power names.
catalysts: Renewable additions, utilisation recovery and tariff stabilisation.
risks: High capex, leverage and weaker returns from falling tariffs.
researchNote: 0836 is more compelling for now.

name: NationGate
thesis: Malaysia's most direct listed AI hardware/manufacturing exposure in this basket.
catalysts: AI server manufacturing and higher-value electronics demand.
risks: Customer/theme concentration, semiconductor cycle and AI-capex sensitivity.
researchNote: Keep separate from defensive grid names.

name: Hibiscus Petroleum
thesis: Malaysia-listed independent upstream producer and a direct crude-price expression.
catalysts: Production growth and higher realised oil prices.
risks: Oil prices, field decline/decommissioning and production interruptions.
researchNote: Use when specifically seeking oil beta.

name: DIALOG Group
thesis: Steadier Malaysian oil-infrastructure exposure through terminals, downstream services and upstream interests.
catalysts: Terminal utilisation, downstream activity and recurring infrastructure earnings.
risks: Project timing and slower upside than direct upstream during oil spikes.
researchNote: Think hydrocarbon toll-road rather than crude-price trade.

name: SLB
thesis: Global upstream-capex play rather than direct oil-price beta, with a small data-centre solutions adjacency.
catalysts: International/offshore activity and upstream spending.
risks: Producer capex cuts, service-price pressure and deep cyclicality.
researchNote: Use when the thesis is upstream capex stays high.

name: Marathon Petroleum
thesis: Direct way to express refining-margin and crack-spread strength, with MPLX adding steadier midstream cash flow.
catalysts: Tight product markets, refinery reliability and buybacks.
risks: Refining margins are highly cyclical.
researchNote: Pair with crack-spread analysis rather than crude price alone.

name: Valero Energy
thesis: Clean large-cap refining-margin play for product tightness and crack-spread strength.
catalysts: Utilisation, product shortages, export economics and capital returns.
risks: Crack-spread compression, recessionary demand and regulatory costs.
researchNote: Margin-cycle exposure, not a crude-price proxy.

name: Powerwell Holdings
thesis: Small-cap Malaysian power-distribution equipment maker supplying switchboards, switchgear, busway and transformers.
catalysts: Data-centre electrical projects and Malaysian infrastructure growth.
risks: Small order book, concentration, execution and DC-cycle sensitivity.
researchNote: Needs full financial-quality review before promotion.

name: Copper complex
thesis: Cleanest metal adjacency to AI and electrification because transformers, cables, motors, generation and transmission all consume copper.
catalysts: Grid expansion, data centres, renewable interconnections and mine-supply constraints.
risks: China demand and global recession can dominate structural demand in the short run.
researchNote: Higher-priority metal than palladium for this theme.

name: Palladium
thesis: Electronics uses exist, but AI linkage is weak; autocatalyst economics remain much more important.
catalysts: Supply disruptions and auto-cycle surprises rather than AI.
risks: EV transition structurally challenges autocatalyst demand.
researchNote: Do not treat as a clean AI thesis.
